findings.issue: Regression test is order-sensitive (I mutation-verified it myself: swapping to catch-all-first -> 404 RED), so it is NOT tautological. BUT it re-registers registerRightsResourcesRoute + registerRightsRoutes by hand rather than importing buildRouter from server.ts. It therefore locks the CONTRACT (resources module before rights module) but would NOT auto-catch a future re-ordering of the real call in server.ts. Same limitation as the sibling CR-9 lock it mirrors.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable (established sibling pattern). Ideal future hardening: assert against the router assembled by buildRouter() so a server.ts re-order regresses automatically.

findings.issue: 401 is most likely a token-timing artifact (I AGREE): shell.jsx:1015 authReady gates first render until the KC bootstrap/refresh completes, so a valid-session boot 401 is unlikely. However the mechanism for a latent race EXISTS: authHeaders() returns {} (no Authorization) whenever getToken() is momentarily null (refresh in flight), and the three admin screens use BARE fetch(authHeaders()), NOT the T-0608 fetchWithAuthRetry self-heal wrapper. A transient no-token window or mid-session expiry would 401 without self-heal. Not a proven non-issue.
findings.suggestion: Non-blocking follow-up: migrate screen-rights.jsx / ra-grant-trail.jsx / users screen fetches to fetchWithAuthRetry (T-0608) so a transient/expired token self-heals instead of surfacing a raw 401.

findings.issue: OUT-OF-SCOPE finding by the builder is a REAL P1 (high plausibility), NOT a false alarm. KC 25.0.6 (docker-compose.yml:52) ships the declarative user profile GA with unmanaged attributes DISABLED by default. createHumanUser sets attributes.actor_type=["human"] via admin REST POST /users, but realm-choros.json has NO userProfile section, so kc-dev-setup.sh step 5 (explicitly designed to declare actor_type via PUT /users/profile) hits its [SKIP] branch -> actor_type stays undeclared/unmanaged -> KC25 silently drops it on admin-API create -> the UI-created user's login token carries no actor_type claim -> verifyClaims (FF-3) rejects -> 401 on everything. Seeded/fixture users work because realm import writes attributes directly (bypasses profile validation) -> the exact seeded-OK vs UI-created-401 asymmetry reported. Corroborated by prior memory T-0638 (realm-reimport wipes actor_type -> 401). Caveat: not live-reproduced; if KC returns 400 instead of silently dropping, createHumanUser maps it to a misleading EMAIL_INVALID. Either way it is a genuine defect for UI-created accounts.
findings.suggestion: Separate task (judge already filing). Fix by adding a userProfile block to realm-choros.json declaring actor_type (options-validated per the kc-dev-setup.sh comment) OR set unmanagedAttributePolicy. NOT fixed here (out of scope for the 404 ordering fix).
